title: streaming: lifecycle controls for client cancel, disconnect handling, reconnect/resume and server timeouts
author: Lina Chen
description: Context: Streaming endpoints experienced a class of flakiness where client-initiated cancels or abrupt TCP disconnects could leave server-side stream state and long-lived model kv-cache pinned, leading to increased memory usage and request stalls. This PR implements a coordinated lifecycle control surface across the API layer, runtime, and gateway to: 1) make client cancel signals explicit and reliable for both HTTP streaming and WebSocket clients, 2) improve disconnect detection and immediate server-side cleanup, 3) enable reconnect and resume semantics for short-lived reconnections (resume token based), and 4) add server-side timeouts and backoff heuristics to prevent runaway KV cache retention. Summary of changes: - API: new StreamingSession object and resume token flow; added cancel semantics to OpenAI-compat streaming API so that libs/clients sending an event: {"type":"cancel"} or terminating a stream will trigger a deterministic cleanup path. - Gateway: explicit lifetime ping/pong and half-close handling for proxy connections; support for the new Resume-Token header and mapping to session IDs. - Runtime: session manager with lease/TTL, reference counting for KV cache, cancellation propagation to model workers, and async cleanup tasks to release caches within 500ms of final cancel/disconnect. - SDK compatibility: OpenAI-compat layer accepts/expands the new cancel and resume events; TS/Python SDKs updated with helper utilities (StreamSession, resume()) and sample usage in docs. - Timeouts: server-side soft timeout (idle between frames) and hard timeout (max session duration) configurable via runtime config with sensible defaults (soft=30s, hard=10m). - Telemetry/Observability: added metrics for sessions_open, sessions_resumed, sessions_cancelled, session_cleanup_duration_ms, and tracing spans for session lifecycle to the console dashboards. Migration notes and rollout: - New behavior is opt-in per-route via route config 'streaming.lifecycle: "enabled"' to allow staged rollout. - For backward compatibility, if lifecycle is disabled, behavior falls back to existing best-effort cleanup. - Resume tokens are opaque; resume window defaults to 60s and is adjustable. - No model changes required. Testing and validation: - Unit + integration tests for cancel propagation, disconnect race conditions, and resume correctness. - Load tests in perf-canary showing <1% p99 latency impact and reduced memory churn under noisy disconnect workloads. - Staging canary with traffic shadowing for 48h before full rollout. Motivation: Production incidents correlated with long-lived sessions after client crashes. This design provides deterministic cleanup and a developer-friendly resume path while preserving OpenAI compatibility. See linked Linear tasks for additional context.
commits_summary: Initial implementation of StreamingSession and session manager
Gateway: add Resume-Token header support and enhanced proxy ping handling
Runtime: cancellation propagation to workers and cache reference counting
SDKs: TypeScript and Python helpers and examples
Tests: unit/integration for cancel/disconnect/resume; added perf canary harness
review_conversation: Ethan Moore: Overall looks good. Two concerns: (1) what happens if resume token is reused maliciously? We should scope tokens to route+client and rotate TTLs. (2) ensure cancellation is propagated even when the worker is busy computing next token.

Lina Chen: Addressed in commit 3/5: tokens are HMAC'd with route id and we store only a short-lived lease; TTL rotation is configurable. Cancellation now posts a cancellation future that the worker checks at safe yield points and we added a best-effort preempt path to interrupt long-running ops.
Marco Alvarez: Can we add an emergency cleanup path in case cleanup task fails? Suggest a periodic scavenger that runs every minute and logs details to Sentry.
Lina Chen: Added scavenger and Sentry instrumentation; explained behavior in docs and added e2e test that simulates cleanup failure.
Priya Nair: Telemetry looks good, please add a dashboard tile for sessions_cancelled / sessions_open ratio and alarm if ratio > 0.6 for 5m.
Lina Chen: Added dashboard and alert config in observability-pack; included runbook note.
tests_and_validation_notes: Integration tests cover cancel->worker propagation, disconnect cleanup, resume token acceptance, and TTL eviction. Added a chaos test in perf-canary that randomly drops connections; observed 70% reduction in leaked kv-cache entries and stable p99 latency in staging shadowed traffic.
release_notes: Server: Add opt-in streaming lifecycle controls for deterministic session cleanup and resume support; configurable timeouts and telemetry. SDKs: helpers for StreamSession and opaque resume token support. Backwards compatible when disabled.
rollout_plan: Stage: enable streaming.lifecycle per-route in staging namespaces; shadow production traffic for 48h; gradual rollout to 10%/30%/100% over 72h with monitoring alerts; fallback toggle to disable lifecycle per-route if issues detected.
migration_instructions: No data migration required. To enable: set route config streaming.lifecycle: "enabled" and optionally tune runtime_defaults.yaml for soft/hard timeouts. Update clients to consume resume token for best UX (optional).
notes: This PR touches runtime/gateway/sdk/docs and requires coordination with platform and SDK teams for the rollout tickets. Created ENG-1492 and ENG-1501 for follow-ups (observability refinements and UX polish).
